summary: Summation No. 13 covers October 1946 in South Korea under the U.S. Army Military Government. The dominant events were the autumn strike wave and riots, centred on Taegu and the Kyongsang provinces, which ended in martial law, a Seoul curfew and three public statements by the Commanding General, USAFIK. Politically, the first elections since annexation chose 45 members of the Korean Interim Legislative Assembly (Ordinance No. 118), the Kim Kyu Sic-Lyuh Woon Hyeung Unification Committee issued seven principles, and a Socialist Labor Party formed. The report also records the settled railroad and marine strikes, the opening of rice collection (1 percent of quota by month end), new ordinances on patents, tariffs, grain mills, film licensing and Korean names, cholera totals of 15,481 cases, repatriation figures, and trade tables for imports from the U.S., China and Japan. Historians will find the official framing of the unrest, press comment, and detailed economic and labor statistics useful.
highlights: Riots that began with the late-September railroad strike spread from Taegu to Seoul, Masan, Chinju, Kaesong and Inchon; at the Taegu stage 44 police were killed and 153 injured, 39 rioters killed and 148 injured, and martial law was invoked.
The Commanding General, USAFIK, issued public statements on 4, 14 and 23 October blaming outside agitators, and a 2200-0600 curfew for Koreans in the Seoul-Yongdong-po area began on 21 October.

Ordinance No. 118 created a 90-member Korean Interim Legislative Assembly, half elected; the first elections gave 15 seats to the Korean Democratic Party, 14 to the National Society, 2 to the Independence Party, 2 to the Cheju-do People's Committee and 12 to independents.

On 7 October the Kim Kyu Sic-Lyuh Woon Hyeung Unification Committee issued seven principles, including land redistribution, nationalization of key industries and reconvening the Joint Commission; the Military Governor announced a limited veto policy on 18 October.

The railroad strike was settled on 26 October (final agreement 12 October, average raise of 200 yen a month) and the Pusan marine strike on 17 October; gasoline shortages immobilized most motor transport.

Fall rice was estimated at 1,779,519 metric tons, 83 percent of the wartime average; by 31 October only 1 percent of the collection quota was in, against a 5 percent schedule, and the Seoul-Inchon ration rose to 277 grams.

October ordinances introduced a Patent Law (No. 91), a 10 percent ad valorem tariff ceiling (No. 116), licensing of grain mills (No. 113) and films (No. 115), and restoration of Korean names (No. 122).

Cholera reached 15,481 cases and 10,043 deaths by 30 October; repatriation had returned 860,534 Japanese and 918,143 Koreans, and the Inchon refugee camp, which shipped out 27,460 refugees, closed on 14 October.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers, title page for No. 13 (October 1946), table of contents of four parts, and list of 27 charts plus a map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Monthly digest: Ordinance No. 118 and the election of the Legislative Assembly, the October riots, rice collection, railroad and marine strikes, repatriation, cholera and Hankul Day.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Ordinances 114 and 118 and the election of 45 assembly members (31 right, 2 left, 12 independents); also the Unification Committee, the Socialist Labor Party, new ordinances and the October riots.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Fall crops 15 percent below normal, alcohol curtailment from 1 November, railroad strike ended 26 October, 311 foreign trade licenses, and Bank of Chosen notes at 12.2 billion yen.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Repatriation totals, closure of the Inchon refugee camp, cholera at 15,481 cases, Seoul National University unrest, Hankul Day, the Korean Olympics and press focus on unification.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics (Legislative Assembly, Unification Committee, nine-party committee) and legal and public safety matters, including the October riots and new ordinances.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Provincial reorganization, 90-member assembly, Military Governor's 18 October veto policy, Unification Committee principles, Joint Korean-American Conference, and Gen. Brown replacing Gen. Arnold.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Ordinance No. 114 abolishes provincial police departments; Ordinance No. 118 sets up the 90-member Assembly; Dr. Chyun Kyu Hong appointed secretary on 14 October.

sections.title: Political Affairs
sections.summary: Election results by province, the seven-point Unification Committee declaration of 7 October, a nine-party left-wing committee, the Joint Conference agenda, and the Socialist Labor Party formed 14 October.

sections.title: Joint Commission and Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: Maj. Gen. Albert E. Brown replaces Maj. Gen. A. V. Arnold as head of the U.S. delegation; 116 foreign nationals registered, including 41 stateless Tartars.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Six bar admissions, price-violation trial rules, Ordinances 91, 113, 115, 116 and 122, riot chronology with casualties, police controversy, 19,407 prison inmates and Coast Guard seizures.

sections.title: Legal and Major Legislation
sections.summary: Trial within 48 hours for price violators, Patent Law, 10 percent tariff ceiling, grain mill and film licensing, and restoration of Korean names by 23 December.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Strikes turned to riots, with martial law at Taegu and a Seoul curfew from 21 October; Gen. Hodge's statements, Military Governor on pro-Japanese police, and Coast Guard seizures of rice smugglers.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources (crops, fisheries, forestry, coal, minerals) and commerce and industry (production, transport, strikes, trade, rationing, prices, finance), with 25 charts.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Grain inspection rules, fall rice at 1,779,519 tons, 14,880 tons of October fish landings, fuel wood shortage, and September coal output of 25,579 tons.

sections.title: Agriculture
sections.summary: Ordinance No. 111 requires inspection of 18 grain varieties; crop estimates, Agricultural Association franchise extension, and an animal census of 2,335,312.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: 14,880 tons landed in six provinces, 45 whales caught, 38,321 registered vessels and 338,238 fisheries workers; boats, nets and fuel in short supply.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: July lumber output of 690,000 board feet, 1946 charcoal at 69,000 tons, 55 trucks allocated for fuel wood, and 645 sawmills.

sections.title: Mining
sections.summary: September coal 25,579 tons, problems at Hwasun and Kyongju mines, graphite 2,370 tons, plus kaolin, pyrophyllite and tungsten concentrates.

sections.title: Section 2. Commerce and Industry
sections.summary: Industrial exhibition, alcohol curtailment, railroad and marine strikes, telephone and postal data, trade with the U.S., China and Japan, rice collection, rationing, price indexes and currency.

sections.title: Industry and Textiles
sections.summary: National Industrial Exhibition opened 19 October, alcohol output curtailed from 1 November, Inchon fertilizer plant closed, 66,152 pounds of cocoons allocated to filatures.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Railroad strike ended 26 October, gasoline shortage halted motor transport, 4,614 ships registered, eight port districts planned, and 89 Seoul streetcars running.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Interzone mail resumed 12 October (119,919 pieces), telephone messages up to 214,035 in August, Mukden cable repaired, JODK power cut to 10 kilowatts.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Strikes in Seoul, Inchon and Kyongsang-pukto; railway settlement with a 200 yen average raise; Pusan marine strike settled 17 October; public works halted by gasoline shortage.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: 311 foreign trade licenses; U.S. imports of 16.8 million dollars to September; October imports from China of 68.5 million yen; Japanese import and export tables.

sections.title: Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Rationed population 6,500,000, Seoul-Inchon ration of 277 grams, 1 percent of rice quota collected, cotton prices set 22 October, cost-of-living differential raised 250 yen, fines raised 50 times.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes of 12,197,703,695 yen, up 856,396,695 yen in October; 26 million yen loan to the Water Utilization Association.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education, culture and religion, and public information: cholera, repatriation, school unrest, the Korean Olympics and press policy.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Refugee flow falling from 28,728 to 3,761, repatriation totals, medical exams, vaccine stocks, UNRRA shipments, and cholera at 15,481 cases and 10,043 deaths.

sections.title: Public Welfare and Repatriation
sections.summary: Kyongsang-pukto relief committee seeking 350 million yen, Seoul low-cost restaurants serving 456,966 meals, Inchon camp closed 14 October, last Chinese repatriation shipment.

sections.title: Hospital Administration and Nursing
sections.summary: Refresher course for government physicians 14-19 October, 160 limited doctors examined, 17 nurses graduated and 230 took national nursing exams.

sections.title: Dental, Veterinary and Nutrition
sections.summary: Seoul dentists' association formed, animal disease cases including 707 of fowlpest, and a book analyzing 414 Korean foods.

sections.title: Supply and Distribution
sections.summary: Smallpox vaccine stock of 873,100 doses; first UNRRA shipment handed to the Soviets 12 October; UNRRA clothing and shoes allocated to five provinces.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: Autumn Cleanup Week from 6 October, cholera at 15,481 cases with highest incidence in the Kyongsang provinces, smallpox control delayed until cooler weather.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University strikes and low faculty pay, Chosen Christian College made a university, 82 new middle schools, Hankul Day, 1946 Korean Olympics, nine missionaries arriving.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Department reorganized into five bureaus, rice and strike publicity, Ordinance No. 115 film licensing, JODK schedule, and Gen. Hodge's 11 October press-freedom statement.

sections.title: Information Programs, Motion Pictures and Radio
sections.summary: Rice program film and pamphlet airdrops, newsreels of the Olympics, three Korean films reviewed, and JODK broadcasting schedule from 17 October.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Gen. Hodge's 11 October statement that there is no censorship; press reaction to the Assembly, unification, Rhee's demand to cancel the Moscow Decision, and the British Foreign Minister's remarks.

sections.title: Map of Korea and back matter
sections.summary: Printed map of Korea (printed page 87), followed by blank pages, a library due-date slip and the back cover.
